ubuntu-24.04-arm.scope: Same-run F64 array comparison: one cached address versus the existing per-element array-data selection. Reuses verified emitted C, checks its recorded hashes, changes only cached load expressions, preserves arithmetic and ownership, and compares result hashes and complete allocation profiles. The compiler optimizes away unused cached-pointer parameters in the control. Both tracing and ARC use identical C flags. Forty samples per binary from eight rotating four-binary batches, after warmup; each binary occupies each position twice. Profiles are separate from timing. This isolates a generated-code change; it is not a C/Rust comparison, whole-program startup measurement or a general zero-cost claim.

Reuses verified emitted C, checks its recorded hashes, changes only cached load expressions, preserves arithmetic and ownership, and compares result hashes and complete allocation profiles. The compiler optimizes away unused cached-pointer parameters in the control. Both tracing and ARC use identical C flags. Forty samples per binary from eight rotating four-binary batches, after warmup; each binary occupies each position twice. Profiles are separate from timing. pairedLoadComparisons.interpretation: Intel macOS ARC cached/per-element ratios were 0.704 and 0.707; Linux ARM64 ARC 0.965 and 0.967. Linux AMD64 tracing ratios were 0.757 and 0.861. ARM macOS ARC changed direction (0.968 then 1.021), while tracing was slower (1.046 then 1.009). Generated ARM tracing loops remove address selection without added loop spills, but still reload array length around root-liveness fences. These two shared-runner experiments do not establish a universal gain or a stable ARM macOS penalty. Keep all slower cases and allocation-inclusive timings.
